focus: Exodus 33 turns on one question after the golden calf: will the LORD Himself still go with His people? The LORD offers an Angel to lead Israel into the land but refuses to go in their midst, the people mourn, Moses meets with the LORD at the tent outside the camp, and his pleading leads to the LORD’s promise of His presence and to Moses’ request, “Please, show me Your glory” (Exodus 33:18).

sections.title: The LORD Will Send an Angel but Will Not Go Among Israel
sections.summary: The LORD tells Moses to lead the people to the promised land and promises His Angel to drive out its inhabitants, “for I will not go up in your midst, lest I consume you on the way” (Exodus 33:3). When the people hear this bad news they mourn, and at the LORD’s command they strip off their ornaments at Mount Horeb.

sections.title: The LORD Speaks with Moses at the Tent Outside the Camp
sections.summary: Moses pitches a tent far outside the camp and calls it the tabernacle of meeting, and the people watch and worship as the pillar of cloud descends at its door. “So the LORD spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend” (Exodus 33:11), and Joshua remains at the tent.

sections.title: Moses Pleads for the LORD’s Presence
sections.summary: Moses asks the LORD, “show me now Your way, that I may know You” (Exodus 33:13), and the LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest” (Exodus 33:14). Moses insists that only the LORD’s going with them sets Israel apart from all other peoples, and the LORD agrees because Moses has found grace in His sight.

sections.title: Moses Asks to See the LORD’s Glory
sections.summary: Moses asks, “Please, show me Your glory” (Exodus 33:18), and the LORD promises to make all His goodness pass before him and proclaim His name, but says, “no man shall see Me, and live” (Exodus 33:20). He will place Moses in the cleft of the rock and cover him with His hand, and Moses will see His back but not His face.

1.brief: The LORD tells Moses to depart with the people and go up to the land He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. God’s promise of the land still stands after the calf.
1.explain:
“Then the LORD said to Moses, ‘Depart and go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought out of the land of Egypt,”

After the golden calf, God tells Moses to lead the people on. He calls them “the people whom you have brought out,” as in 32:7. God’s distance from the people is felt in the words.

“to the land of which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘To your descendants I will give it.”

God’s oath to the fathers still stands. Moses had appealed to it (32:13). God’s promise of the land still stands after the calf.

2.brief: The LORD says, “I will send My Angel before you,” and He will drive out the peoples of the land. Guidance and victory are still offered.
2.explain:
“And I will send My Angel before you,”

God will send “My Angel” to lead them (32:34). In this passage, the Angel is offered in place of God’s own presence among the people (33:3).

“and I will drive out the Canaanite and the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.”

God will still give victory over the nations. Guidance and victory are still offered.

3.brief: Israel is to go up to a land flowing with milk and honey, “for I will not go up in your midst, lest I consume you on the way,” because they are stiff-necked. The land is promised, but God’s own presence is withheld because of their sin.
3.explain:
“Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey;”

The good land is still theirs to enter.

“for I will not go up in your midst, lest I consume you on the way, for you are a stiff-necked people.”

But God will not travel among them. The reason is mercy and judgment together. Because they are “stiff-necked,” God’s holy presence among them would destroy them. The land is promised, but God’s own presence is withheld because of their sin.

4.brief: When the people hear this “bad news,” they mourn, and no one puts on his ornaments. The people understand that losing God’s presence is a grievous loss.
4.explain:
“And when the people heard this bad news, they mourned,”

The people call it “bad news.” They understand that the land without God is a great loss. They “mourned.”

“and no one put on his ornaments.”

They do not wear their “ornaments,” jewelry and finery. The people understand that losing God’s presence is a grievous loss.

5.brief: The LORD tells them, “You are a stiff-necked people,” warns that He could consume them in a moment, and orders them to take off their ornaments while He decides what to do. Their mourning is to express repentance before God.
5.explain:
“For the LORD had said to Moses, ‘Say to the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people.”

God repeats His charge: “stiff-necked.”

“I could come up into your midst in one moment and consume you.”

God warns that He could destroy them “in one moment.” Their sin makes His nearness dangerous.

“Now therefore, take off your ornaments, that I may know what to do to you.”

God commands them to remove their ornaments “that I may know what to do to you.” This is a call to repentance. Removing ornaments was a sign of humility and mourning. The ornaments may also recall the gold given for the calf (32:2–3).

6.brief: The children of Israel strip off their ornaments at Mount Horeb. The people humble themselves before God.
6.explain:
“So the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments by Mount Horeb.”

The people obey. They humble themselves before God at “Mount Horeb.” The text implies they did not wear them from then on.

7.brief: Moses pitches a tent far outside the camp and calls it the tabernacle of meeting, and everyone who seeks the LORD goes out to it. The distance of the tent from the camp shows the separation sin has caused.
7.explain:
“Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and called it the tabernacle of meeting.”

Moses sets up “his tent” “outside the camp, far from the camp.” The tabernacle had not yet been built. This was a temporary tent of meeting. Its distance from the camp shows the separation sin has caused. God would not dwell in their midst.

“And it came to pass that everyone who sought the LORD went out to the tabernacle of meeting which was outside the camp.”

Anyone who wanted to seek the LORD had to go “outside the camp.”

8.brief: Whenever Moses goes out to the tent, all the people rise and stand at their tent doors watching him until he enters. The people watch Moses go to meet with God.
8.explain:
“So it was, whenever Moses went out to the tabernacle, that all the people rose,”

Whenever Moses walks to the tent, “all the people rose.”

“and each man stood at his tent door and watched Moses until he had gone into the tabernacle.”

They stand at their doors and watch until he enters. The people watch Moses go to meet with God.

9.brief: When Moses enters the tent, the pillar of cloud descends at its door, “and the LORD talked with Moses.” God’s presence meets Moses at the tent.
9.explain:
“And it came to pass, when Moses entered the tabernacle, that the pillar of cloud descended and stood at the door of the tabernacle,”

When Moses enters, “the pillar of cloud descended.” God’s visible presence comes down to meet him.

“and the LORD talked with Moses.”

God speaks with Moses at the tent. God’s presence meets Moses there.

10.brief: All the people see the pillar of cloud at the door and rise and worship, each at his own tent door. The people worship from a distance as God meets Moses.
10.explain:
“All the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the tabernacle door,”

The whole camp can see the cloud at the tent.

“and all the people rose and worshiped, each man in his tent door.”

The people “worshiped,” each at his own tent door. They worship from a distance as God meets Moses.

11.brief: “So the LORD spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend,” and when Moses returns to the camp, Joshua does not depart from the tent. Moses enjoys a close friendship with God, and young Joshua stays at the place of meeting.
11.explain:
“So the LORD spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.”

God speaks with Moses “face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” The phrase describes close, direct, personal communication. It does not mean Moses saw God’s face, as 33:20 makes clear. Moses enjoys a close friendship with God.

“And he would return to the camp, but his servant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, did not depart from the tabernacle.”

Moses goes back to the camp, but “Joshua” stays at the tent. Young Joshua remains at the place of meeting.
11.notes: Numbers 12:8 says God speaks with Moses face to face and plainly, and Deuteronomy 34:10 says no prophet arose like Moses, “whom the LORD knew face to face.”

12.brief: Moses tells the LORD that He has told him to bring up the people but has not said whom He will send, though He has said, “I know you by name, and you have also found grace in My sight.” Moses appeals to his relationship with God.
12.explain:
“Then Moses said to the LORD, ‘See, You say to me, ‘Bring up this people.’ But You have not let me know whom You will send with me.”

Moses presses God. He has been told to lead the people but does not know who will go with him. An Angel has been promised, but Moses wants more.

“Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found grace in My sight.”

Moses appeals to his relationship with God. God knows him “by name,” personally and intimately, and he has “found grace” in God’s sight.

13.brief: Moses prays, “show me now Your way, that I may know You,” and asks God to remember that “this nation is Your people.” Moses wants to know God Himself and pleads for the people as God’s own.
13.explain:
“Now therefore, I pray, if I have found grace in Your sight, show me now Your way, that I may know You and that I may find grace in Your sight.”

Moses asks, “show me now Your way, that I may know You.” He wants to understand God’s ways so that he may know God Himself more deeply.

“And consider that this nation is Your people.”

Moses reminds God whose people these are. He will not let God call them only Moses’ people (33:1). Moses pleads for the people as God’s own.
13.notes: Psalm 103:7 says, “He made known His ways to Moses, His acts to the children of Israel.”

14.brief: God answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” God promises Moses His own presence and rest.
14.explain:
“And He said, ‘My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”

God answers, “My Presence will go with you.” The Hebrew reads literally My face will go. God promises not just an Angel but Himself. He also promises “rest,” the settled peace of the promised land and of life with Him. Jesus said, “Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest” (Matthew 11:28). Hebrews 4:9–10 speaks of the rest that remains for God’s people.

15.brief: Moses says, “If Your Presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here.” Moses would rather stay in the wilderness than go on without God.
15.explain:
“Then he said to Him, ‘If Your Presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here.”

Moses would rather stay in the wilderness than go on without God. The land without God’s presence is not worth having.

16.brief: Moses asks how it will be known that he and the people have found grace unless God goes with them, “So we shall be separate, Your people and I, from all the people who are upon the face of the earth.” God’s presence is what sets Israel apart from every other nation.
16.explain:
“For how then will it be known that Your people and I have found grace in Your sight, except You go with us?”

Moses asks how anyone will know that God has accepted them unless He goes with them.

“So we shall be separate, Your people and I, from all the people who are upon the face of the earth.”

God’s presence makes Israel “separate,” distinct from every other nation. Their laws, their land, and their worship do not set them apart as much as God’s presence among them.

17.brief: The LORD says, “I will also do this thing that you have spoken; for you have found grace in My sight, and I know you by name.” God grants Moses’ request out of His grace and personal knowledge of him.
17.explain:
“So the LORD said to Moses, ‘I will also do this thing that you have spoken;”

God grants the request. He will go with them.

“for you have found grace in My sight, and I know you by name.”

God grants it because of His grace and His personal knowledge of Moses. God answers Moses’ intercession.

18.brief: Moses asks, “Please, show me Your glory.” Having received God’s promise, Moses longs to see God Himself more fully.
18.explain:
“And he said, ‘Please, show me Your glory.”

Moses asks for more. “Please, show me Your glory.” Having received God’s promise, Moses longs to see God Himself more fully.

19.brief: God answers, “I will make all My goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you,” adding that He will be gracious and compassionate to whom He will. God reveals His glory as His goodness and His name.
19.explain:
“Then He said, ‘I will make all My goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you.”

God answers by promising His “goodness” and His “name.” God reveals His glory as His goodness and His character, proclaimed in His name. This promise is fulfilled in 34:5–7.

“I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.”

God declares His freedom in mercy. He shows grace and compassion according to His own will, not because anyone has earned it.
19.notes: Paul quotes this verse in Romans 9:15–16 to show that mercy “is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy.”

20.brief: God says, “You cannot see My face; for no man shall see Me, and live.” Even Moses’ closeness to God has limits.
20.explain:
“But He said, ‘You cannot see My face; for no man shall see Me, and live.”

God sets a limit. “You cannot see My face.” No sinful human could survive the full sight of God’s glory. Even Moses’ closeness to God has limits.

21.brief: The LORD says, “Here is a place by Me, and you shall stand on the rock.” God makes a place for Moses beside Himself.
21.explain:
“And the LORD said, ‘Here is a place by Me, and you shall stand on the rock.”

God makes a place for Moses “by Me,” on a rock. God prepares a safe place near Himself.

22.brief: While His glory passes by, God will put Moses in the cleft of the rock and cover him with His hand. God both reveals Himself and protects Moses.
22.explain:
“So it shall be, while My glory passes by, that I will put you in the cleft of the rock,”

God will put Moses “in the cleft of the rock,” a crevice in the mountain.

“and will cover you with My hand while I pass by.”

God will “cover” him “with My hand.” God both reveals Himself and protects Moses.

23.brief: God will take away His hand, and Moses will see His back, “but My face shall not be seen.” Moses will see a real but limited vision of God’s glory.
23.explain:
“Then I will take away My hand, and you shall see My back;”

After God passes, Moses will see “My back.” This is human language for a real but limited disclosure. Moses truly sees God’s glory as He passes by, though not His face. It is not a description of God’s body.

“but My face shall not be seen.”

The full glory of God remains hidden. Moses will see a real but limited vision of God’s glory.
23.notes: Elijah later stood at the same mountain, Horeb, and heard God in a still small voice (1 Kings 19:8–13).
